criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies defense cost advancement timing mismatch
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 8 table contrasts Agreement 30-day advancement (§5) with Policy 60-day advancement after invoices (§9.3).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Analyzes cash flow / bridging implications of advancement timing gap
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the Company floats at least 30 days of every invoice cycle before reimbursement, and the director floats 60 days in a Side A scenario.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies broader 'Proceeding' definition vs. narrower 'Claim' definition
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 5 contrasts the broad 'Proceeding' definition (threatened, informal investigations) with the narrower 'Claim' definition, which requires a named formal investigation, subpoena or Wells notice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Notes informal investigations / preliminary inquiries fall outside D&O coverage
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo explains that informal inquiries, voluntary requests and threatened actions trigger advancement but are not Claims, and illustrates this with the 2023 SEC inquiry.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies fines and penalties coverage gap
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 6 says Loss excludes fines and penalties except where insurable under the most favorable law, while Agreement §1(g)/§2 expressly indemnifies Fines.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Explains Company bears uninsured exposure for regulatory fines
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo calls these Company-funded, uninsured obligations; the matrix lists civil penalties as indemnifiable but uninsured; it also notes the insurer-discretion qualifier.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies Insured vs. Insured exclusion gap with indemnification
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 3 details the IvI exclusion and its carve-backs (derivative, employment, whistleblower) and contrasts it with Agreement §3 indemnifying direct Company claims.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Explains scenario where Company owes indemnification without D&O recovery
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo describes Company-initiated fiduciary and clawback claims, including post-change-of-control suits, that are excluded under §5.2 while the Agreement indemnifies the related Expenses (Gap 16).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies dual settlement consent requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 9 identifies Company consent under Agreement §7(d) and separate Insurer consent under Policy §7.2.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Explains potential conflict between Company and Insurer consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo explains misaligned consents: the Company consents or is deemed to consent without Insurer approval, so there is no reimbursement; it recommends the Company not withhold consent merely because the Insurer has not consented.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006a: Identifies D&O policy conduct exclusion requires final non-appealable adjudication
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo repeatedly notes that the Conduct Exclusion requires a final, non-appealable adjudication.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006b: Identifies indemnification agreement uses DGCL § 145 good faith standard with determination process
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies the Agreement's DGCL §145 good faith/best-interests standard, its presumption and clear-and-convincing burden, and the Independent Counsel and deemed-approval determination process, and contrasts it with the Policy's adjudication-based exclusion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Analyzes asymmetry scenarios between the two standards
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo does not analyze divergent outcomes, such as denial of indemnification under the good-faith determination while D&O coverage continues, or the reverse; Gap 11 only addresses venue and lead-in.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies extended reporting period vs. indefinite indemnification duration gap
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 2 contrasts the Agreement's indefinite survival with claims-made coverage and the 12/24-month Discovery Period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Explains exposure for former directors after discovery period expires
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo explains that on lapse or non-renewal, former directors keep only a contractual right against a weakened Company; it flags this as high exposure and ties it to the incoming directors.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies contribution cap under indemnification agreement
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 15 identifies the §10 12-month compensation cap but does not discuss how it interacts with D&O policy limits.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Analyzes exposure when insurance limits are exhausted
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 7 notes that indemnification becomes an uninsured Company cost after exhaustion, but it does not analyze a claim exceeding the $50M capacity in terms of the contribution provision, the Indemnitee cap and unlimited Company exposure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies subrogation conflict between policy and agreement
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo treats subrogation as 'Aligned' and does not identify a potential circular subrogation conflict between Policy §12.2 and Agreement §13.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Explains circular subrogation practical implications
criteria_results.reasoning: No analysis of the practical implications of circular subrogation is provided.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies ERISA claims gap — Side B exclusion leaves Company uninsured
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 12 notes that the ERISA exclusion applies to Sides B/C with a carve-back for Side A only, that the Agreement covers plan service and ERISA excise taxes, and that plan-fiduciary indemnification is uninsured.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: References ERISA § 410(a) or explains why ERISA claims create unique D&O coverage gaps
criteria_results.reasoning: No reference to ERISA §410(a) or to ERISA limits on indemnification; the memo only notes this Policy's exclusion and recommends a fiduciary policy, without explaining why ERISA claims are a distinctive gap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies absence of tail coverage obligation for change of control
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 1 identifies that §11 has a maintenance covenant but no change-of-control tail obligation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Explains change-of-control tail risk and market practice
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo explains that an acquiror cancels or folds in the program, leaving former directors uninsured, and describes six-year tail market practice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-monetary relief / compliance costs gap
criteria_results.reasoning: Gap 6 identifies the Policy's exclusion of costs of complying with injunctive/non-monetary relief, versus Agreement Expenses including costs of complying with court orders and consent decrees.
